HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Vacancy Details

All 6 posts are in the Unreserved (UR) category. The number of vacancies is provisional and may be increased or decreased based on actual requirement.

S. No. Post Name No. of Posts
1 Scientist/Engineer SD – Post Code 01 (Bioinstrumentation / Biophysics / Medical Physics) 1 (UR)
2 Scientist/Engineer SD – Post Code 02 (Developmental Biology / Biotechnology) 1 (UR)
3 Scientist/Engineer SD – Post Code 03 (Cellular & Molecular Biology / Cell Biology) 1 (UR)
4 Scientist/Engineer SD – Post Code 04 (Computational Biology / Systems Biology / Bioinformatics) 1 (UR)

6 Scientist/Engineer SD – Post Code 06 (Biomedical Engineering / Biomedical Sciences – Bio-imaging/Signal Processing) 1 (UR)

Candidates can apply for more than one post code if they meet the eligibility for each, though HSFC reserves the right to conduct interviews for two or more posts simultaneously as per administrative need. Where discipline names overlap (as in Post Codes 05 and 06), candidates should apply only against the post code matching their essential and pre-requisite qualification.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is assessed as on the crucial date of 30.08.2026. Only candidates who hold the required qualification by this date can apply.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Qualification (Post-Code Wise)

Post Code Discipline Essential Qualification Pre-requisite Qualification
01 Bioinstrumentation / Biophysics / Medical Physics Ph.D. in Bioinstrumentation, Biophysics or Medical Physics ME/M.Tech/MS in Biomedical-Instrumentation, Medical Imaging & Informatics, Healthcare Informatics, Biomedical Engineering or Bioengineering (60% marks / 6.5 CGPA) AND BE/B.Tech in any field (65% marks / 6.84 CGPA)
02 Developmental Biology / Biotechnology Ph.D. in Developmental Biology or Biotechnology ME/M.Tech/MS in Biotechnology, Bioscience & Bioengineering, Biochemical Engineering or Biological Sciences (60% / 6.5 CGPA) AND BE/B.Tech in any field (65% / 6.84 CGPA); OR BS-MS dual degree in Biological Sciences (60% / 6.5 CGPA)
03 Cellular & Molecular Biology / Cell Biology Ph.D. in Cellular & Molecular Biology or Cell Biology MSc in Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Cell and Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Genetics or Life Sciences (60% / 6.5 CGPA) AND BSc in any field (60% / 6.5 CGPA); OR BS-MS dual degree in Biological Sciences (60% / 6.5 CGPA)
04 Computational Biology / Systems Biology / Bioinformatics Ph.D. in Computational Biology, Systems Biology or Bioinformatics ME/M.Tech/MS in Biomedical Engineering, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Bioscience & Bioengineering or Biochemical Engineering (60% / 6.5 CGPA) AND BE/B.Tech in any field (65% / 6.84 CGPA); OR BS-MS dual degree in Biological Sciences (60% / 6.5 CGPA)
05 Biomedical Engineering / Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering or Biomedical Sciences with thesis in biomechanics, human movement, musculoskeletal modeling or equivalent ME/M.Tech/MS in Biomechanics, Biomechanical Engineering or Biomedical Engineering (60% / 6.5 CGPA) AND BE/B.Tech in any field (65% / 6.84 CGPA)
06 Biomedical Engineering / Biomedical Sciences Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering or Biomedical Sciences with thesis in bio-imaging, signal processing, bioinformatics or equivalent ME/M.Tech/MS in Biomedical Engineering, Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Bioscience & Bioengineering, Medical Imaging & Informatics or Biomedical Signal Processing (60% / 6.5 CGPA) AND BE/B.Tech in any field (65% / 6.84 CGPA)

Additional qualification conditions:

  • The Ph.D. and Master's/Bachelor's qualification must be from a recognized university/institute.
  • Candidates with degrees from foreign universities must submit an equivalency certificate from the Association of Indian Universities (AIU) at the time of interview.
  • The ME/M.Tech/MS/MSc/BE/B.Tech/BSc/BS-MS qualification must have been completed within the stipulated duration prescribed by the university.
  • Candidates who completed a professional course through Open and Distance Learning (ODL) are not eligible.
  • Where CGPA is converted to a percentage, or vice versa, ISRO's own eligibility criteria apply; conversion of CGPA to percentage using a university formula is not permitted to determine eligibility, and rounding-off of marks is not allowed.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Age Limit

The upper age limit for all post codes (01 to 06) is 35 years as on the crucial date, 30.08.2026. Serving Central Government employees, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen are eligible for age relaxation as per extant Government of India rules.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Salary

Selected candidates will be placed in Level-11 of the Pay Matrix (Rs. 67,700 – Rs. 2,08,700), with approximate gross emoluments of Rs. 67,700 per month plus admissible allowances.

Post Pay Level Approx. Gross Emoluments
Scientist/Engineer SD (Post Code 01–06) Level-11 (Rs. 67,700 – Rs. 2,08,700) Rs. 67,700 per month + admissible allowances

In addition to Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA) and Transport Allowance are payable as per extant rules. Employees are covered under the National Pension System/Unified Pension Scheme, along with medical facilities for self and dependents, subsidized canteen, quarters facility (in lieu of HRA), Leave Travel Concession, Group Insurance and House Building Advance, as admissible under DOS/Central Government orders.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Application Fee

There is no application fee for the Scientist/Engineer 'SD' posts (Post Codes 01–06).

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Selection Process

Selection is based on the online application submitted through the ISRO Live Register portal:

  • Initial screening of applications to shortlist candidates for interview.
  • The prescribed qualification is the minimum requirement and does not by itself make a candidate eligible for interview or selection.
  • Final selection is based purely on performance in the Personal Interview.

Candidates also have the option to give the interview in Hindi.

How to Apply for HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the ISRO Live Register portal at www.isro.gov.in and go to the "Career" tab.
  2. Register or update your existing registration on the Live Register portal.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, entering correct details in all mandatory (*) fields.
  4. Apply only against the post code matching your essential and pre-requisite qualification.
  5. Upload the required photo, signature and qualification certificates as specified.
  6. Submit the application on or before 30.08.2026 (1700 hrs) and take a printout of the submitted application for future reference.

Candidates registered under the National Career Service (NCS) portal and meeting the eligibility conditions may also visit the ISRO website and follow the same application procedure.

HSFC Scientist/Engineer SD Apply Online

Applications are accepted only online through the ISRO Live Register portal; physical/postal applications are not entertained. No documents need to be sent by post or email.

The Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA), an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, has released a notification (Advt No. ADA:ADV-138:2026, dated 03.08.2026) for the engagement of meritorious Indian Nationals as Project Assistant-I on a tenure basis. The ADA Project Assistant-I Recruitment 2026 drive covers 111 tentative vacancies across seven engineering disciplines: Computer Science, Electronics & Communication, Aeronautical, Electrical & Electronics, Mechanical, Metallurgy, and Civil Engineering.

Eligible candidates who hold a first-class engineering degree (or equivalent, as per the qualification pathway applicable to each discipline) can register online at https://ada.gov.in up to 13th August 2026, 1700 hrs. Selection is through either an interview only, or shortlisting by a written test followed by an interview, depending on the qualification route chosen. The written test and interview will be conducted in Bangalore, and selected candidates will be engaged on tenure for an initial period of two years.

ADA Project Assistant-I Selection Process

The selection method depends on the qualification pathway a candidate falls under, as shown in the Qualification table above:

  • Interview Only: Applicable to candidates with a valid GATE score, M.E/M.Tech from an IIT/NIT, or (for Computer Science and Electronics & Communication Engineering) B.Sc + M.Sc with a valid GATE/NET score.
  • Shortlisting by Written Test followed by Interview: Applicable to candidates qualifying through other routes, such as B.E/B.Tech with M.E/M.Tech, B.E/B.Tech with 2 years of relevant experience, or B.E/B.Tech alone.

The written test will follow the same syllabus as GATE for the relevant discipline and will have negative marking for wrong answers. Candidates are advised to bring a scientific calculator to the written test. Both the written test and interview will be conducted in Bangalore, on dates published on the ADA website based on the number of registered candidates.

How to Apply for ADA Project Assistant-I Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official ADA website at https://ada.gov.in and register online for the Project Assistant-I engagement, selecting the relevant Engineering Discipline and qualification criteria.
  2. Complete the online registration on or before 13th August 2026, 1700 hrs.
  3. Separately fill the application form in the prescribed format, affix a recent passport-size photograph on the top right corner of the first page, and keep it ready along with originals and self-attested copies of all supporting documents.
  4. Frequently check the ADA website for the confirmed written test/interview date, as the tentative dates (16th, 23rd, or 30th August 2026) may be finalised based on the number of registered candidates.
  5. Report for the written test/interview in Bangalore on the notified date, carrying the duly filled application form, original documents, self-attested copies, original Aadhaar card, a scientific calculator (for the written test), and an NOC from the employer if currently employed in a Government department/PSU/Autonomous Body.

Note: Online registration alone does not constitute a complete application. Candidates must still bring a duly filled application form along with all relevant supporting documents when reporting for the written test/interview.

DGQA Technician Selection Process 2026

Selection is done through a Written Test followed by a Trade Test - there is no interview.

  • Written Test: Objective type, Multiple Choice Questions only; no negative marking for wrong answers; duration 90 minutes; 100 questions for 100 marks.
Part Subject Questions Marks
(i) General Intelligence and Reasoning 25 25
(ii) General Awareness 25 25
(iii) English Language and Comprehension 25 25
(iv) Numerical Aptitude 25 25
- Total 100 100

Question papers for Parts (i), (ii), and (iv) are set in English and Hindi; Part (iii) is in English only. Candidates are shortlisted for the Trade Test based on written test marks and category of reservation. The Trade Test carries 100 marks, with a minimum qualifying mark of 40. The final merit list is prepared post both tests, based on Trade and Establishment. In case of a tie, resolution is by (1) older date of birth ranked higher, then (2) higher marks in Numerical Aptitude, then Reasoning, then General Awareness.

How to Apply for DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026

DGQA Technician Recruitment 2026 has no apply-online option. The application must be sent physically by Registered or Speed Post only.

  1. Fill the application in the prescribed format (Appendix 'A'), typed in English on A4 size paper.
  2. Attach the Admit Card in the prescribed format - Appendix 'B' for Technician (Semi Skilled) or Appendix 'C' for Technician (Skilled) - submitted in duplicate.
  3. Affix one self-attested passport-size photo on the application form, and one self-attested photo on each of the two admit card copies (three photos total).
  4. Enclose a self-addressed envelope (30cm x 12cm) affixed with a postal stamp of Rs. 55/- for admit card despatch.
  5. Clearly superscribe the envelope: "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF [Technician (Semi Skilled) / Technician (Skilled)] AND CATEGORY [SC/ST/OBC/UR]".
  6. Candidates already working in Government Service or a Public Sector Undertaking must route their application through proper channel, with a No Objection Certificate from their Head of Office; applications without this NOC are summarily rejected without further communication.
  7. Send the complete application by Registered/Speed Post to: Controllerate of Quality Assurance (Systems), DGQA Technical Complex, Manovikas Nagar P.O., Secunderabad – 500009.

Applications received after the closing date, even due to postal delay, are rejected summarily and no correspondence is entertained.

The pay scale for the post is ₹40,000–1,40,000.

RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Vacancy Details 2026

RITES Recruitment 2026 covers a total of 24 Assistant Manager (Mechanical) vacancies, distributed across categories as shown below. One post is reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) on a horizontal basis, and the total includes backlog vacancies.

RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Eligibility Criteria 2026

Candidates wondering whether they qualify for RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Recruitment 2026 can check the educational qualification, experience, and age limit requirements below.

Educational Qualification

Candidates must hold a full-time Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering/Technology in Mechanical, Production, Production & Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical/Railways, Mechatronics & Automobile, or a combination of the above disciplines in part or whole.

  • UR/EWS candidates (and SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PWD candidates applying against unreserved posts) need a first-class degree or a minimum of 60% marks.
  • Reserved category candidates (SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PwBD, as applicable) need a minimum of 50% marks for consideration against reserved posts.
  • The degree must be recognized by AICTE and awarded by a University established under an Act of Parliament/State legislature, or a Deemed University under the UGC Act, 1956. Sections A & B of the Institution of Engineers (India) examination, treated as equivalent to a degree by the Government of India, are also accepted.
  • If the marksheet does not show a class/division or percentage, candidates must submit the conversion formula issued by their university; if no such formula exists, an authorized undertaking is required, and a CGPA of 6 on a 10-point scale will then be treated as 60%.

Experience Requirement

Candidates need a minimum of 2 years of post-qualification experience in production or mechanical maintenance or other mechanical engineering areas, gained while working at a project site, factory, or plant. Training (except on-the-job training), internship, teaching, academic work, fellowship, or Ph.D. research experience will not be counted. However, Apprenticeship training under the Apprenticeship Act, 1961, in the relevant discipline will be considered towards the minimum experience, subject to fulfilment of other eligibility conditions.

Age Limit

The upper age limit for RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Recruitment 2026 is 32 years as on the last date of application submission (17 August 2026).

For the Mechanical discipline, the post is identified suitable for candidates with locomotor disability categories OA, OL, OAL, BL, Leprosy Cured, and Acid Attack Victims, with functional classifications S, ST, BN, W, SE, MF, C, R, W & RW. Persons with disabilities belonging to an identified category can apply even where no vacancy is specifically reserved for them, and will be considered by the general standard of merit.

RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Selection Process 2026

Selection for RITES Recruitment 2026 involves three stages - a written test, document scrutiny, and an interview - with a fixed weightage split between the written test and interview.

1. Written Test

  • The written test consists of 125 objective-type questions carrying one mark each, for a duration of 2.5 hours.
  • There is no negative marking; no marks are deducted for incorrect answers.
  • PwBD candidates are eligible for a compensatory time of 50 minutes.
  • A minimum of 50% marks is required for UR/EWS candidates (45% for SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PwBD against reserved posts) to be considered further.

2. Document Scrutiny

Based on the written test result and the number of vacancies, RITES will scrutinize the documents submitted by candidates, and shortlisted candidates will be called for an interview preceded by verification of original documents. It is the candidate's responsibility to upload documents that substantiate all claims made in the application form.

3. Interview

  • Candidates are called for interview in the ratio of 1:6 to the number of vacancies.
  • Weightage: Written Test – 60%, Interview – 40% (Technical & Professional proficiency: 30, Personality, Communication & Competency: 10). Total: 100%.
  • A minimum of 60% marks in the interview is required for UR/EWS candidates (50% for SC/ST/OBC(NCL)/PWD against reserved posts) to be placed on the panel. There is no minimum qualifying mark required in the aggregate.
  • Candidates can appear for the selection process in either Hindi or English.
  • Based on RITES's discretion, the written test and/or interview may be conducted at Regional Offices, which will be communicated with the call letters.

Appointment of selected candidates is subject to being found medically fit as per RITES Rules and Standards of Medical Fitness for the post.

Written Test Venue & Centres

Candidates must give two preferences for their choice of written test centre at the time of online application. RITES will make efforts to allot a preferred centre but reserves the right to allot a different one.

RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Written Test Syllabus

The written test syllabus for the Mechanical discipline covers core mechanical engineering subjects, similar in scope to the GATE Mechanical syllabus.

  • Applied Mechanics and Design: Engineering Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials, Theory of Machines, Vibrations, Machine Design.
  • Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Sciences: Fluid Mechanics, Heat Transfer, Thermodynamics, Power Engineering, I.C. Engines, Refrigeration & Air-conditioning, Turbomachinery.
  • Materials, Manufacturing and Industrial Engineering: Engineering Materials, Casting/Forming/Joining Processes, Machining & Machine Tool Operations, Metrology & Inspection, Computer Integrated Manufacturing, Production Planning & Control, Inventory Control, Operations Research.
  • Manufacturing Processes: Metal casting, metal forming, metal joining/welding, welding metallurgy, powder metallurgy, non-destructive testing.
  • Testing of Materials: Non-destructive testing (ultrasonic, radiography, magnetic particle, eddy current, dye penetration), physical testing (tensile, hardness, impact, bend, shear, fatigue, creep), chemical testing, metallography.
  • Material Science: Thermal, chemical, electrical, magnetic and mechanical properties of materials, structure of metals, corrosion, heat transfer, air compressors, air conditioning.

RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Candidates checking the RITES Assistant Manager salary can note that the pay scale for the post is ₹40,000–1,40,000, with pay fixed at the minimum of the scale for new appointees.

  • Employees appointed on a regular basis from other PSUs or Government organizations (Central/State/Banks/Autonomous Body), who applied through proper channel or submitted an NOC at the time of interview, are eligible for protection of pay (Basic + DA) as per company policy.
  • In addition to Basic Pay, selected candidates will get DA, fixed/variable allowances, Performance Related Pay, medical facilities, HRA/lease accommodation, and a superannuation package including PF contribution, Gratuity (as per the Gratuity Act), and Post Retirement Medical Scheme.
  • Other benefits include leave as per leave rules, Maternity/Paternity Leave, medical facility, Group Insurance, and Leave Encashment, as applicable to regular employees.

Candidates switching from 8th CPC CDA pay scales to 4th PRC IDA pay scales on appointment/absorption in RITES will be entitled to the benefit of only one fitment, with final fixation done after implementation of the 4th PRC report, if any.

Documents Required for RITES Assistant Manager Recruitment 2026

Candidates must upload the following documents during online application, substantiating their eligibility and claims:

  • Certificates and mark statements of all academic/professional qualifications for all semesters/years (10th, 12th, Diploma/Graduation/Post-Graduation as claimed)

  • PwBD Certificate as per the latest format (if applicable)
  • Any other document supporting the candidature and claims made in the application

Candidates called for document verification must additionally carry a printed, signed copy of the application form (with registration number) along with self-attested scanned copies of the same documents, plus one recent passport-size colour photograph, in the prescribed order.

How to Apply for RITES Assistant Manager (Mechanical) Recruitment 2026

  1. Ensure you satisfy the necessary conditions and requirements before applying.
  2. Apply online through the registration format available in the Career Section of the RITES website, www.rites.com.
  3. Note down the "Registration No." generated on top of the online form for all further communication with RITES.
  4. Carefully fill in the "Identity Proof" details, and ensure the same document is available for production at later stages of selection.
  5. Upload all the required documents under the "Upload Document" section, ensuring scanned copies are clear and visible.
  6. Make the online payment under the "Make Payment" section, and download the final application form after successful payment.
  7. Keep a copy of the submitted application form and carry it at the time of selection, if called.

Applications without successful fee payment will be treated as incomplete and summarily rejected. Candidates can apply for any number of vacancies separately, but only one application per vacancy is allowed, and an application once submitted cannot be altered.

RITES Assistant Manager Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Candidates working in Government organizations (Central/State/Autonomous Body)/PSUs/PSBs on a regular basis must apply through proper channel; if applying directly, they must bring a No Objection Certificate (NOC) at the time of interview for pay protection, transfer of gratuity/leave, and joining benefits. NOC submitted after the interview date will not be considered.
  • SC/ST/OBC-NCL candidates must furnish caste certificates in the prescribed Annexure I/II format, valid as on the last date for application submission; OBC-NCL candidates must additionally submit a non-creamy layer declaration (Annexure III) at document verification.
  • EWS candidates must possess an Income and Asset Certificate in the Government of India format, valid as on the last date of application submission (valid for FY 2026-27).
  • Hard copies of documents are not to be sent to RITES by post or courier.
  • Candidates must bring two duly filled copies of Annexure A (Documents Submission Checklist) along with supporting documents in chronological order at the time of document verification/selection.
  • The date of acquiring a qualification is the earliest of: the last day of the month in which the final exam was held (or the exact exam date, if stated), the date of declaration of result, the date of issuance of the marksheet, or the date of issuance of the degree - with no relaxation on this account.
  • Where a specialization is required in the qualifying degree, candidates must submit a certificate from their University/Institution clearly specifying the specialization.
  • The appointment will initially be on probation for one year from the date of joining; confirmation depends on performance and verification of submitted certificates/documents.
  • Selected candidates are liable for posting anywhere in India and abroad, as per company requirements.
  • Candidates must clear a screening test for confirmation of service at the end of probation; failure may lead to extension of probation.
  • No employee's application will be forwarded for outside jobs until they complete 2 years of service at RITES.
  • Any corrigendum/addendum to the advertisement will be displayed only on www.rites.com.
  • No fares, TA, or DA will be paid for the selection process. Legal jurisdiction for any dispute is Delhi.

IBPS Clerk Eligibility Criteria

The eligibility conditions below are the basic criteria for applying. IBPS clarifies that qualifying in the CRP and being provisionally allotted to a bank does not guarantee employment - the concerned bank retains the final say on appointment.

Criteria Details
Nationality Citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 01.01.1962, or a person of Indian origin migrated from specified countries with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India
Age (as on 01.08.2026) Minimum 20 years, Maximum 28 years (born not earlier than 02.08.1998 and not later than 01.08.2006)
Educational Qualification (as on 21.08.2026) A Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a University recognised by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the Central Government
Local Language Proficiency Candidates must be proficient in reading, writing, speaking and understanding the specified/opted local language of the State/UT they apply for (see Local Language Proficiency Test section)
Computer Literacy Mandatory - a Certificate/Diploma/Degree in computer operations, or having studied Computer/IT as a subject in High School/College

IBPS Clerk Qualification for Ex-Servicemen

Ex-Servicemen who do not hold the above civil qualification are eligible if they are matriculate Ex-Servicemen who obtained the Army Special Certificate of Education (or the equivalent Navy/Air Force certificate) after completing at least 15 years of service in the Armed Forces, with the certificate dated on or before 21.08.2026.

IBPS Clerk Age Limit

The standard age limit is 20 to 28 years as on 01.08.2026. Relaxation in the upper age limit is available to reserved categories as follows:

Age relaxation for SC/ST/OBC candidates is available cumulatively with only one of the other relaxation categories listed above (Point II 3 to 5 of the notification), not with more than one.

The application fee (inclusive of GST) must be paid online between 01.08.2026 and 21.08.2026:

  • SC/ST/PwBD/ESM/DESM candidates: ₹175
  • All other candidates: ₹850

Bank transaction charges for online payment are to be borne by the candidate. Payment can be made via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards/Mobile Wallets, or UPI. A correction fee of ₹200 (inclusive of GST) applies if a candidate uses the Edit Window to modify the submitted application.

The Customer Service Associate is eligible for allowances and perquisites as per the rules of the participating bank in force from time to time. Exact take-home pay after allowances is not specified in the notification, since it varies bank to bank.

IBPS Clerk Selection Process

Selection for CRP CSA-XVI is a two-tier process consisting of an Online Preliminary Examination and an Online Main Examination, followed by a qualifying Local Language Proficiency Test before joining.

Test Medium No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time Allotted

There is a penalty of one-fourth (0.25) of the marks assigned to a question for each wrong answer in both the Preliminary and Main Examinations. No penalty applies to unattempted questions. Candidates must clear individual cut-offs in each test as well as an overall cut-off. Only marks obtained in the Main Examination are considered for the final merit list; Preliminary Exam marks are used only for shortlisting.

Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the State/UT they apply for. Candidates who have studied that language up to Class 10 or above are exempt from a separate test. Others must clear a qualifying (marks-based) Local Language Proficiency Test conducted after the Main Exam/provisional allotment but before joining - failing this test means disqualification from the process.

Provisional Allotment

Shortlisted candidates are provisionally allotted to one of the participating banks based on merit-cum-preference and State/UT-wise vacancies reported to IBPS. A reserve list of approximately 30% of vacancies in each category may also be maintained, though this does not guarantee eventual allotment. Provisional allotment is subject to identity verification and the candidate being found medically fit and otherwise eligible by the allotted bank.

How to Apply for IBPS Clerk Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply online only - no other mode of application is accepted.

  1. Visit the official IBPS website www.ibps.in and open the "CRP CSA" link, then click "Click Here to Apply Online for CRP – Customer Service Associates (CRP-CSA-XVI)".
  2. Click "Click Here for New Registration" and enter basic details to generate a provisional registration number and password (also sent by email/SMS).
  3. Upload the required scanned documents: photograph, signature, left thumb impression, a handwritten declaration, SSC/SSLC/10th standard or equivalent certificate, and the certificate mentioned in Clause K(ix) if applicable - as per the specifications in Annexure IV of the notification.
  4. Carefully fill in all sections of the online application form using the "Save and Next" facility to verify details before final submission, since most fields cannot be edited after submission.
  5. Indicate the State/UT for which you want to be considered for provisional allotment - this choice is irrevocable once submitted.
  6. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online through the integrated payment gateway (Debit Card/Credit Card/Internet Banking/IMPS/Wallets/UPI).
  7. On successful payment, take a printout of the e-receipt and the completed application form for your records.

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), through the ISRO Centralised Recruitment Board (ICRB), has released the ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 Notification on 27 July 2026 on the official website isro.gov.in. A total of 244 vacancies have been announced for Assistant, Junior Personal Assistant (JPA), Upper Division Clerk (UDC), and Stenographer posts under Level 4 of the Pay Matrix.

Candidates who possess a Graduation with at least 60% marks (or the prescribed Diploma qualification for certain posts) and satisfy the prescribed age limit of up to 28 years (with relaxation for reserved categories as per Government rules) are eligible to apply for these vacancies. The online application process will commence on 27 July 2026 (10:00 AM) and will remain open until 16 August 2026 (11:55 PM).

Candidates can download the ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF and apply online through the direct links provided below in this article. They can also check the detailed eligibility criteria, vacancy details, selection process, application fee, salary, and other important information before submitting their applications.

Refund is not considered if a candidate fails to appear for the written test/CBT.

ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Written Test

A single objective-type paper of 150 minutes duration (with compensation time for PwBD candidates) will be conducted at 38 venues across India, including Agartala, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Chandigarh/Mohali, Chennai, Dehradun, Delhi, Ernakulam, Gorakhpur, Gurugram, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Indore, Jaipur, Jammu, Jodhpur, Kanpur, Kavaratti, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mangaluru, Mumbai, Mysore, Nagpur, Patna, Port Blair, Pune, Raipur, Ranchi, Shillong, Tiruchirapalli, Thiruvananthapuram, Varanasi, Vijayawada, and Visakhapatnam.

Post Parts Questions / Marks Duration Qualifying Marks
Assistant / UDC (Post 1, 3 & 5) A: General English, B: Quantitative Aptitude, C: General Intelligence & Reasoning, D: General Knowledge 50 Q / 50 Marks each (200 total) 150 minutes 50% (UR), 40% (Reserved categories against notified reserved vacancies)
JPA / Stenographer (Post 2, 4 & 6) A: English Language & Comprehension, B: General Intelligence & Reasoning, C: Quantitative Aptitude & General Knowledge A: 100 Q/100 Marks, B: 50 Q/50 Marks, C: 50 Q/50 Marks (200 total) 150 minutes 50% (UR), 40% (Reserved categories against notified reserved vacancies)

Marking pattern: +1 for correct answer, -0.25 for wrong answer. No TA is paid for attending the written test.

Skill Test

Based on written test performance, candidates are shortlisted for the skill test in the ratio of 1:5 (maximum) to the category-wise number of vacancies.

Post Skill Test Components Passing Criteria
Assistant / UDC Computer Literacy Test (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint) 60% (UR), 50% (Reserved categories)
JPA / Stenographer Computer Literacy Test + Stenography Test (300 words @ 60 wpm shorthand, 30 minutes computer transcription) Computer Literacy: 60% (UR) / 50% (Reserved); Stenography: max 10% mistakes (UR) / max 12% mistakes (Reserved)

Final selection is based on marks scored in the written test, from among candidates who qualify in the skill test. In case of a tie, tie-breakers are applied in order: (a) marks in General Intelligence & Reasoning (Post 1,3,5) or English Language & Comprehension (Post 2,4,6); (b) date of birth, with the older candidate preferred.

ISRO ICRB Last Date to Apply Online

  • The online application process for ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 started on 27 July 2026 at 10:00 AM and will remain open until 16 August 2026 at 11:55 PM.
  • Candidates who meet the prescribed eligibility criteria are advised to complete the registration process well before the last date to avoid last-minute technical issues.
  • Applications are accepted online only through the official ISRO website. Applicants should ensure that all required documents, including their photograph, signature, and applicable certificates, are uploaded correctly before submitting the application.
  • The application fee must also be paid online on or before 16 August 2026 for the application to be considered complete.

Direct Link to Apply Online for ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026

ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 How to Apply

  • Applications are accepted online only, through the ISRO website, between 27-07-2026 (10:00 AM) and 16-08-2026 (11:55 PM).
  • Candidates may apply for more than one post, subject to conditions. A candidate may apply for different posts under the same or different zones but cannot apply for the same post in different zones. Candidates applying for multiple posts must select the same written test centre.
  • Email ID and mobile number are mandatory in the online application; all hall tickets, call letters, and communications will be sent only via registered email/SMS, with no hard copies sent separately.
  • Candidates registered under the National Career Services (NCS) portal and meeting eligibility conditions may follow the same application process on the ISRO website.
  • Candidates must upload a recent colour passport-size photograph (not older than 6 months, .jpg/.jpeg, 20–50 KB, 200x230 pixels preferred) and signature (.jpg/.jpeg, 10–20 KB, 140x60 pixels preferred), along with SC/ST/Disability/Ex-servicemen certificates where applicable.
  • Applications not conforming to the notified requirements, or incomplete applications, will not be considered.

ISRO ICRB Recruitment 2026 Remuneration

  • Selected candidates will be appointed as Assistant / Junior Personal Assistant / Upper Division Clerk / Stenographer in Level 4 of the Pay Matrix.
  • Minimum basic pay: ₹25,500 per month.
  • Additional allowances: Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), and Transport Allowance as per extant Central Government rules.
  • Employees will be governed by the New Pension Scheme.
  • Other benefits: medical facilities for self and dependents, subsidised canteen, limited quarters facility (in lieu of HRA), Leave Travel Concession, Group Insurance, and House Building Advance, as admissible per Central Government orders.

Important Instructions

  • Candidates employed under Central/State Government, PSUs, or Autonomous Bodies must submit a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer at the time of the Skill Test. Failure to submit the original NOC will result in the candidate not being permitted to appear for the Skill Test, and TA will not be paid.
  • PwBD candidates applying for reserved posts must submit a self-attested Disability Certificate in the prescribed format, indicating percentage of disability (minimum 40% relevant disability required for reservation eligibility), issued by a duly constituted Medical Board.
  • OBC candidates must possess a valid OBC certificate (non-creamy layer, in the prescribed proforma) as on the last date of application. EWS candidates must possess a valid Income and Asset Certificate for financial year 2026–2027.
  • Candidates attending the Skill Test will be reimbursed second-class railway fare (to and fro, shortest route) from the city indicated in the application to the Skill Test venue. No TA is payable for the Written Test.
  • All original documents must be produced at the time of the Skill Test in support of details furnished online. False information will result in disqualification from the Skill Test, and TA will not be paid.
  • Answer keys will be published on the ISRO website within three working days of the written test. Objections, with valid justification, may be raised only through the designated link within 5 days of publication; objections received after this window or through any other mode will not be considered.
  • Appointees are liable to be posted or transferred to any Centre/Unit of the Department of Space/ISRO at any time, based on requirement. The number of vacancies indicated is provisional, and ISRO reserves the right to increase, decrease, or not fill the posts without assigning any reason. The posts are temporary but likely to continue.
  • Any court case or legal matter arising from this recruitment falls under Bangalore, Karnataka jurisdiction. Canvassing in any form will result in disqualification.
  • Candidates are advised NOT to take cognizance of any fake offer of appointment for jobs in ISRO.
  • In case of ambiguity between the Hindi and English versions of the notification, the English version shall be treated as final.

AIIMS NORCET 11 Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must satisfy the following essential qualification and registration requirements to appear in NORCET-11. Eligibility must be fulfilled on or before the closing date of online registration, i.e. 13 August 2026.

AIIMS Nursing Officer Educational Qualification

Candidates must meet either of the following two eligibility routes:

  • Route I: B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing / B.Sc. Nursing from an Indian Nursing Council or State Nursing Council recognized institute or university, OR Post-Certificate/Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from a recognized institute/university; AND registration as a Nurse and Midwife with the State or Indian Nursing Council.
  • Route II: Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery (GNM) from a recognized institute/board/council; registration as a Nurse and Midwife with the State or Indian Nursing Council; and two years of experience in a minimum 50-bedded hospital acquired after obtaining the essential qualification (i.e., after completing residency, declaration of result, and council registration).

AIIMS NORCET 11 Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection is made through a two-stage Computer-Based Test (CBT):

  • Stage I – NORCET Preliminary: A 90-minute qualifying exam with 100 MCQs (100 marks) - 20 questions on General Knowledge & Aptitude and 80 on Nursing subjects. There is negative marking of 1/3 mark per wrong answer. This stage only qualifies candidates for Stage II and is not used for final merit.
  • Stage II – NORCET Mains: A 180-minute exam with 160 case-scenario-based MCQs (160 marks) covering the nursing syllabus, testing clinical skill competency. Negative marking of 1/3 mark per wrong answer applies. Final merit is based solely on Stage II performance.

Qualifying marks for Stage I are 50 percentile (UR/EWS), 45 percentile (OBC), and 40 percentile (SC/ST), with a further 5 percentile relaxation for PWBD candidates. Qualifying marks for Stage II are 50% (UR/EWS), 45% (OBC), and 40% (SC/ST), with a similar 5% PWBD relaxation. Candidates qualifying in Stage I, up to 5 times the seats per category, are called for Stage II. Ties in Stage II merit are resolved sequentially by fewer negative marks in Stage II, higher Stage I score, fewer negative marks in Stage I, older date of birth, and finally alphabetical order of name.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

For posts up to Scale III, selection may comprise Online Examination, Group Discussion (if required), and/or Personal Interview, depending on the number of applicants. For posts in Scale IV, V, and VI, selection may comprise Group Discussion (if required), any other test/assessment, and/or Personal Interview. The Bank reserves the right to add, cancel, or modify the selection method for any notified post.

Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, and English Language sections are qualifying in nature - marks in these are not counted toward final merit. All tests except English Language are available bilingually (English and Hindi). Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for General/EWS categories, 35% for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD), subject to the Bank's discretion. There is a penalty of 25% of the marks assigned to a question for each wrong answer; unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Personal Interview

A Personal Interview of 100 marks assesses academic and job knowledge, power of expression, clarity of thought, leadership qualities, communication skills, and suitability for the post. Minimum qualifying marks: 50 for General/EWS, 45 for Reserved Category (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD). Candidates are called for interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of vacancies (subject to change at the Bank's discretion).

Final Merit

Final selection is based on the aggregate marks of Online Examination and Personal Interview (or Personal Interview alone, or GD/other assessment plus Personal Interview, depending on which stages are conducted), prepared in descending order category-wise, up to the number of vacancies. In case of a tie, the candidate senior in age (earlier date of birth) is ranked higher.

The State Bank of India (SBI) has released the notification for recruitment of Junior Associates (Customer Support & Sales) under a Special Recruitment Drive for SC/ST/OBC Backlog Vacancies (Advertisement No. CRPD/CR/SPLDRIVE/2026-27/16). Online registration is open from 7 August 2026 to 27 August 2026. This article explains the exam pattern for Prelims and Mains, the Local Language Proficiency Test, marking scheme, and selection process exactly as given in the official notification.

Note on syllabus: The official notification specifies the names of the test sections, number of questions, marks, and duration for each phase, but it does not publish a topic-wise syllabus. Wherever this article lists sub-topics for a section, it is clearly marked as a general guide and not an officially notified syllabus. If a detail is not available in the notification, this article states that explicitly instead of assuming it.

SBI Junior Associates (Clerk) Syllabus 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Organisation State Bank of India (SBI)
Post Junior Associate (Customer Support & Sales)
Recruitment Type Special Recruitment Drive for SC/ST/OBC Backlog Vacancies
Advertisement No. CRPD/CR/SPLDRIVE/2026-27/16
Total Vacancies 1,538 (SC: 207, ST: 1,219, OBC: 112)
Application Mode Online only
Selection Stages Preliminary Exam → Main Exam → Local Language Proficiency Test
Official Website https://sbi.bank.in/

Important Dates

Event Date
Start of online registration and fee payment 7 August 2026
Last date for online registration and fee payment 27 August 2026
Preliminary Examination Tentatively September 2026
Main Examination Tentatively October/November 2026

SBI has stated these exam dates are tentative. Candidates should keep checking the official careers page for the confirmed schedule and call letter release.

Also Read: SSC JHT PST 2026 Date

SBI Junior Associate Exam Pattern 2026

The selection process has three stages: Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, and (where applicable) a Local Language Proficiency Test. Both online tests carry negative marking of 1/4th mark for every wrong answer.

Phase I: Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Prelims is an objective test of 100 marks and 1 hour total duration, split into three separately timed sections. There is no sectional cut-off, but the Bank shortlists candidates for Mains based on aggregate marks (approximately 10 times the number of vacancies per category, subject to availability).

S.No. Test Name Medium of Exam No. of Questions Max. Marks Duration
1 English Language English 30 30 20 minutes
2 Numerical Ability English/Hindi (as per state) 35 35 20 minutes
3 Reasoning Ability English/Hindi (as per state) 35 35 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 Hour

Phase II: Main Examination Pattern

The Main Exam is an objective test of 200 marks over 2 hours 40 minutes, with four separately timed sections. Only the aggregate marks obtained in the Main Examination are used to prepare the final merit list Prelims marks are not added at this stage.

S.No. Test Name Medium of Exam No. of Questions Max. Marks Duration
1 General/Financial Awareness English/Hindi (as per state) 50 50 35 minutes
2 General English English 40 40 35 minutes
3 Quantitative Aptitude English/Hindi (as per state) 50 50 45 minutes
4 Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude English/Hindi (as per state) 50 60 45 minutes
Total 190 200 2 Hr. 40 min.

Candidates must score minimum qualifying marks on aggregate, as decided by the Bank; there are no individual sectional qualifying marks, and sectional marks are not maintained separately.

Phase III: Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

Provisionally selected candidates who have not studied the specified local language of the applied state in Class 10 or 12 must appear for the LLPT after Main Exam qualification but before joining. Candidates who submit a 10th/12th mark sheet showing the local language as a subject are exempted from this test.

S.No. Test Pattern Section No. of Passages No. of Questions Max. Marks
1 Non-Verbal Test Objective 3 15 15
1 Non-Verbal Test Subjective 3 15 15
2 Verbal Test - - 20

Candidates who fail to qualify the LLPT will not be offered appointment.

SBI Junior Associate Syllabus 2026 (Section-wise Guide)

The notification does not release a detailed, topic-wise syllabus it only names the test sections shown above. Based on the officially named sections, the following are the broad areas typically covered under each section for this kind of clerical-cadre banking exam. Treat this as a general study guide, not an official syllabus document.

Prelims Sections

  • English Language: Reading comprehension, cloze test, para jumbles, error detection, fill in the blanks, vocabulary-based questions.
  • Numerical Ability: Simplification, number series, quadratic equations, data interpretation, arithmetic problems (percentage, profit & loss, average, ratio, time & work, simple/compound interest).
  • Reasoning Ability: Puzzles, seating arrangement, syllogism, inequality, coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, alphanumeric series.

Mains Sections

  • General/Financial Awareness: Current affairs, banking and financial awareness, static general knowledge.
  • General English: Comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, sentence correction, and para-based questions at a slightly higher difficulty than Prelims.
  • Quantitative Aptitude: Data interpretation, data sufficiency, arithmetic word problems, number series, simplification/approximation.
  • Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude: Advanced puzzles and seating arrangement, logical reasoning, plus basic computer knowledge (fundamentals, MS Office, internet, and banking-related computer terms).

Also Read: Bihar BPSC Auditor OMR Sheet 2026

How to Apply

  • Visit the official SBI careers page: https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings
  • Locate and open the "Special Recruitment drive for Junior Associates 2026" link.
  • Download and carefully read Advertisement No. CRPD/CR/SPLDRIVE/2026-27/16.
  • Register online with a valid email ID and mobile number.
  • Fill in the application form and upload the scanned photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and hand-written declaration.
  • Pay the application fee (if applicable) using debit card, credit card, or internet banking.
  • Submit the form and save/print the system-generated application form for your records (this printout is not to be sent to SBI).

Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for vacancies in one State/UT only and can appear for the test only once under this recruitment project.
  • There is no provision for Inter-Circle or Inter-State transfer, except intra-state transfer between Delhi Circle & Lucknow Circle (Uttar Pradesh) and between Mumbai Metro Circle & Maharashtra Circle (Maharashtra), subject to the Bank's extant guidelines.
  • No changes or corrections to submitted application particulars, including category, will be entertained under any circumstances.
  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, calculators, and similar devices are strictly prohibited inside the examination premises.
  • A wait list of up to 50% of vacancies (state-category wise) will be maintained and released quarterly, valid for one year from the date of declaration of the final result.
  • SBI reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely at any stage.
  • SBI has clarified it does not endorse any external coaching platform or consultancy claiming to guarantee selection; candidates should rely only on the official career portal.

PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Qualification

The candidate must have passed at least the Higher Secondary School Certificate examination (H.S.C. - 12th) or an equivalent diploma.

Age Limit

Minimum 18 years to maximum 38 years, reckoned as on 01-08-2026. For candidates already appointed on a contract basis in various agencies/organizations under the bank, who have a minimum of 3 years' work experience as on 01-08-2026, the upper age limit is relaxed up to 43 years.

Domicile Requirement

The candidate must be an original resident of Pune district for at least the last 15 years, supported by a valid Domicile Certificate issued after 2018 by a competent authority. 100% of posts will be filled on a priority basis from candidates who are original residents of Pune district. Married women candidates who are original residents outside Pune district may also apply if they submit their husband's original Pune district domicile certificate along with a marriage registration certificate from a competent authority.

Candidates must also be physically fit for the physical movement-related duties of the Shipai post, and must submit a declaration under the Maharashtra Civil Services Rules, 2005 (small family declaration).

PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

The exam fee is Rs.1,650/- plus 18% GST and service charge. This fee is non-refundable under any circumstances and cannot be carried forward or reserved for any other exam or selection. Payment must be made online only - via UPI, Debit Card (RuPay/Visa/Master Card/Maestro), Credit Card, Internet Banking, or Mobile Wallets (GPay, PhonePe, BHIM, etc.). Registration is not considered complete until the exam fee is paid.

PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026 Salary

Selected eligible candidates will be appointed on a temporary probationary basis for 6 months. During this probation period, candidates will be paid a consolidated salary of Rs.12,000/- per month. After confirmation, the applicable pay scale is:

Pay Scale (Shipai): 195-10-225-12-265-14-345-16-435-19-530-24-650-29-795-34-965-34-1000-34-1170, plus allowances and facilities applicable as per the bank's rules.

PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Offline Written Exam

The written exam carries 70 marks and is conducted offline using the OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) method. The question paper is objective and multiple-choice, in Marathi medium, with 70 questions of 1 mark each, to be completed in 75 minutes. The subject-wise mark distribution is as follows:

Subject Marks
Basic information on the three-tier structure of agricultural credit 20
Banking and Cooperation 15
General Knowledge and Current Affairs 15
Agriculture and Rural Economy 10
Intelligence/Aptitude Test 10
Total 70

Document Verification

Based on merit in the written exam, candidates eligible for interview will be shortlisted in a ratio of 1:3 against the vacant posts (the shortlist is published seat-number wise, not marks-wise, on the bank's website). Eligible candidates' original certificates for the required educational qualification and other eligibility criteria will be preliminarily verified by bank officials before the interview; original documents must be produced at this stage.

Interview

Candidates found eligible in document verification will be called for an interview carrying 30 marks. The interview assesses the candidate's personality, physical capability, communication skills, basic knowledge of the bank, local knowledge of Pune district, service attitude, and the fundamental principles and etiquette of cooperation. Candidates absent for the interview will be disqualified from final selection.

Final Selection List and Waiting List

The candidate's written exam marks and interview marks are added together out of a total of 100 marks, and the final result is declared in merit order. A waiting list is prepared at 20% of the vacant posts and remains valid for one year from the date the final selection list is declared. In case of a tie in marks, priority is given first by age seniority, then by experience, then alphabetically by surname (in English).

How to Apply for PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026

  1. Applications are accepted only online, through the bank's official websites: https://www.pdcc.bank.in/careers and https://www.punedccbank.com. No other mode of application (email, post, or hand delivery) is accepted.
  2. Review the detailed information and instructions on the website, then click "NEW REGISTRATION" to begin the online application.
  3. Fill in all details carefully and completely, as per the eligibility conditions; no supporting documents need to be attached at this stage, but information filled cannot be changed once submitted.
  4. Upload a scanned photograph (3.5cm x 4.5cm, JPG/JPEG, 20KB–50KB) and a scanned signature in black ink on white paper (1.5cm x 3.5cm, JPG/JPEG, 10KB–20KB).
  5. Upload a scanned copy of the Domicile Certificate and Aadhaar Card (JPG/JPEG format, 20KB–50KB each) - this is mandatory.
  6. Proceed to the payment gateway and pay the exam fee online; registration is not complete without fee payment.
  7. Take a printout of the completed application form along with the e-receipt and fee payment details, and keep it safe until the recruitment process is complete.

A candidate cannot submit more than one application; multiple applications will be rejected during scrutiny and the candidate excluded from the selection process. Candidates who have previously applied for this post through any other mode must submit a fresh online application for this recruitment process.

PDCC Bank Shipai Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • If any information filled or documents attached are found false, fabricated, or misleading, or if material information is found concealed, the candidature or appointment will be cancelled immediately.
  • Any attempt to seek recommendation or exert pressure from any official/authority during the recruitment process will result in the candidate being declared ineligible and excluded from the process at any stage.
  • Candidates must be personally present for the written exam, document verification, and interview.
  • The bank reserves the right to change the process/procedure at any time; any such changes will be published in local newspapers or on the bank's website, and individual applicants will not be informed separately.
  • The written exam will primarily be held at centres in Pune city, though other centres within the district may be used if needed, and the exam may be conducted in more than one session depending on the number of candidates.
  • Candidates must have knowledge of Marathi, Hindi and English.
  • The bank has not appointed any publication agency, YouTube channel, or Telegram channel for guidance related to this recruitment or exam - any such claims should be considered unauthorized.
  • Any dispute regarding this recruitment process falls under the jurisdiction of Pune courts only.

Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) has released KRCL Recruitment 2026 (Employment Notification No. CO/P-R/02/2026, dated 31.07.2026) inviting online applications for 201 vacancies across 12 Non-Executive posts in Civil, Signal & Telecommunication (S&T), Operating, Electrical, Mechanical, and Commercial departments.

The posts include Junior Engineer (Civil), Track Maintainer, Senior Section Engineer (S&T and Mechanical), ESTM-III, Section Controller, Station Master, Goods Train Manager, Assistant Loco Pilot, Junior Engineer (Mechanical), Technician-III (Mechanical), and Commercial Supervisor. The online application window will open tentatively during the last week of August 2026, with the exact date to be published on the KRCL website 7 days in advance. The Computer Based Test (CBT) is tentatively scheduled for September 2026. Eligible candidates - land losers, Employment Exchange-registered candidates along the Konkan Railway route, and domiciles of Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka - can apply through the official website, www.konkanrailway.com.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Eligibility to Apply

KRCL Recruitment 2026 is open to the following categories of candidates:

  • Land Loser Candidates: Candidates whose land was acquired for construction of the Konkan Railway Line between Roha (Maharashtra) and Thokur (Karnataka), irrespective of the percentage of land lost. The land loser and/or their spouse, son, daughter, grandson, or granddaughter are eligible under the landloser quota.
  • Employment Exchange Registered Candidates: Domiciles of Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka with valid employment exchange cards registered along the Konkan Railway route (Raigad, Sindhudurg, and Ratnagiri districts of Maharashtra; Goa State; Uttara Kannada, Udupi, and Dakshina Kannada/South Kannada districts of Karnataka).
  • Other Domicile Candidates: Candidates domiciled in the States of Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka (not covered above).
  • KRCL Employees: Serving KRCL employees who have completed at least 3 years of regular service.

Note: Recruitment in the erstwhile Group-D post - Track Maintainer - is limited to eligible Land Loser candidates only.

Preference in Recruitment

Candidates securing the minimum qualifying marks are given preference for recruitment in the following order:

  1. Land Loser candidates (first preference)
  2. Candidates registered in Employment Exchanges along the KR route (second preference)
  3. Candidates domiciled in Maharashtra, Goa, or Karnataka, and KRCL employees (third preference)

Candidates must declare their status (Land Loser/Employment Exchange/Domicile) at the time of application; this choice is final. The second and third panels are operated only after exhausting the panel of eligible land losers.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Reservation Policy

This notification provides Vertical Reservation for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, and EWS, and Horizontal Reservation for Ex-Servicemen (Ex.SM) and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD).

  • EWS Reservation: Candidates not covered under SC/ST/OBC-NCL reservation, whose family gross annual income is below Rs. 8 lakh and who do not own specified categories of land/property, can claim EWS reservation with a valid Income & Asset Certificate.
  • Note: EBC and EWS are different categories - EBC candidates get fee concession only, not job reservation.
  • Horizontal Reservation: Ex-Servicemen and PwBD reservations are included within the post-wise vacancies shown above, irrespective of social community. Ex.SM and PwBD candidates can also apply against unreserved vacancies of posts not exclusively earmarked for them (PwBD candidates only where the post is indicated as suitable for their disability), and are eligible for age relaxation and fee exemption.
  • PwBD Categories: VI (Visually Impaired: Blind/Low Vision), HI (Hearing Impaired: Deaf/Hard of Hearing), LD (Locomotor Disability: One Arm/One Leg/One Arm-Leg/Dwarfism) - subject to a minimum of 40% disability. One Commercial Supervisor post is reserved for PwBD candidates.
  • EWS, SC, ST, and OBC-NCL candidates who qualify without relaxed standards will not be adjusted against reserved vacancies and will be considered under UR.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Exam Pattern (CBT)

The recruitment process varies by post group:

  • Section Controller, Station Master, Assistant Loco Pilot: CBT → Computer-Based/OMR-based Aptitude Test → Document Verification (DV) → Medical Examination. Merit is prepared with 70% weightage to CBT marks and 30% to Aptitude Test marks.
  • Senior Section Engineer (Mechanical/S&T), Junior Engineer (Civil/Mechanical), Goods Train Manager, Commercial Supervisor, Technician-III (Mechanical), ESTM-III: CBT → Document Verification → Medical Examination.
  • Track Maintainer: CBT → Document Verification → Physical Efficiency Test (PET) → Medical Examination.

The CBT is of screening nature with negative marking - one mark is deducted for each wrong answer. Questions are set in five languages: English, Hindi, Marathi, Konkani, and Kannada (the Aptitude Test for SCOR/SM/ALP is in English and Hindi only).

How to Apply for KRCL Recruitment 2026

Interested and eligible candidates can apply online for KRCL Recruitment 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Visit the official KRCL website, www.konkanrailway.com, once the application link goes live (tentatively last week of August 2026).
  2. Register your name on the portal; a Registration Number will be generated and sent via registered email and mobile number, along with a password and application link.
  3. Activate the link to access the application form and fill in personal, educational, and category details, carefully selecting your post-wise preference (this cannot be changed once submitted).
  4. Pay the prescribed examination fee online for each CBT Examination Group selected, using Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, or UPI.
  5. Upload the required scanned documents - photograph, signature, and category certificates (if applicable).
  6. Review all entries carefully, then submit the application before the closing date.
  7. Keep a printed copy of the submitted online application for future reference - do not send it to KRCL by post.

Candidates are advised to apply only through the official KRCL website and to be cautious of fake websites and job racketeers, as KRCL has not appointed any agents or coaching centres on its behalf.

KRCL Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for one or more posts in a single application, in order of preference; once exercised, post preference is final and cannot be changed.
  • KRCL will allot only one post to a selected candidate, based on preference, merit, vacancy position, and qualifying the selection stages - no request for a lower-preference post will be entertained after allotment.
  • Serving Government/PSU employees may apply directly but must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer at the time of DV, failing which their candidature will be cancelled.

  • Candidates must ensure their mobile number and email ID are active throughout the recruitment process, as all communication will be via SMS and email only.
  • Any candidate found using unfair means, impersonation, or furnishing false information will be disqualified and debarred from future KRCL examinations, and is liable for legal action.
  • KRCL reserves the right to change the number of vacancies, cancel the recruitment process in part or full, and reject applications without assigning reasons.

RRB Ministerial & Isolated Categories Recruitment 2026: Vacancy Details

The CEN 08/2025 notification covers 312 vacancies across various Ministerial and Isolated Category posts. Some of the posts under this recruitment, along with their qualification requirements, are listed below. This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of every post under the notification — candidates should refer to the official CEN 08/2025 notification PDF for the complete post-wise and RRB-wise vacancy breakup.

How to Download the RRB Ministerial & Isolated Categories Answer Key 2026?

  1. Visit the official website of your respective RRB region, or use the common portal link.
  2. Look for the notification link titled "CEN No. 08/2025 - Ministerial and Isolated Categories Answer Key 2026" under the Latest Updates or Answer Key/Objection section.
  3. Click the link, which will redirect to the login page.
  4. Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password in the login fields.
  5. Click "Login" to view your recorded responses, question paper, and the provisional answer key.
  6. Use the "Save/Print" option to download the answer key and response sheet as a PDF.

Candidates are advised to take a printout of both the answer key and their response sheet for offline review.

How to Calculate Marks Using the RRB MI Answer Key?

The RRB Ministerial & Isolated Categories CBT carries 100 marks for 100 questions. Use the following marking scheme to estimate your score:

  • Correct Answer: +1 mark
  • Incorrect Answer: -1/3 (0.33) mark deducted
  • Unattempted Question: 0 marks

Formula: Total Marks = (Number of Correct Answers × 1) - (Number of Wrong Answers × 0.33)

How to Raise Objections Against the RRB MI Answer Key 2026?

  1. Log in to the official answer key portal using your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password.
  2. Locate the "Raise Objection" or "Challenge Answer Key" option on your dashboard.
  3. Select the specific question ID and the answer option you believe is incorrect.
  4. Upload a valid justification or supporting reference (textbook page, authoritative source, etc.) for each challenged question. Objections without proof are not considered.
  5. Pay the objection fee of Rs. 50 per question (plus applicable bank charges) via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or Net Banking.
  6. Submit the form and save the confirmation/acknowledgement for future reference.

Particulars Details

Objection Window 31 July 2026 (11:55 PM) to 7 August 2026 (11:55 PM)
Payment Modes Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, Net Banking

Objections submitted after the closing date, or through email/post, will not be entertained.

Important Instructions

  • Only the provisional answer key is currently available; scores calculated using it are estimates, not final.
  • The final answer key will be released after review of all valid objections received during the window.
  • The official result will be based on the final answer key, not the provisional one.
  • Use only official RRB regional websites or the authorized login portal to access the answer key — avoid unofficial third-party links for login.
  • Keep your Registration Number and Date of Birth/Password handy before attempting to log in.

RRB Group D City Intimation Slip and Admit Card 2026

  • The Exam City & Date Intimation Slip, along with the Travel Authority download option for SC/ST candidates, is released around 10 days before each individual exam date on the official RRB regional websites.
  • The first City Intimation Slip was released on 24th July 2026.
  • The E-Call Letter (Admit Card) becomes available approximately 4 days before the date mentioned in the City Intimation Slip.
  • The first Admit Card release is reported as 31st July 2026.
  • Since the CBT is being conducted in multiple phases through August 2026, City Intimation Slips and Admit Cards will continue to be released in batches closer to each phase's exam dates.

RRB Group D CBT Exam Pattern 2026

The Computer Based Test consists of objective-type multiple-choice questions with negative marking for wrong answers.

Aadhaar-Based Biometric Authentication: Important Instructions

The official notice places strong emphasis on Aadhaar verification for CEN 09/2025 candidates:

  • Candidates must carry either their original Aadhaar card or a printout of e-verified Aadhaar.
  • Candidates who have not completed Aadhaar verification are advised to do so in advance by logging into the official portal with their registered credentials.
  • Even candidates who verified Aadhaar during the application stage must ensure their Aadhaar status is "unlocked" in the UIDAI system before arriving at the centre. A locked Aadhaar can cause avoidable delays during registration on exam day.
  • Candidates are advised to check their Aadhaar lock/unlock status on the official UIDAI portal a few days before the exam.

  4. Download and take a printout of the City Intimation Slip and, later, the Admit Card.
  5. Verify your Aadhaar unlock status on the UIDAI portal before the exam date.

RRB Group D 2026: What Candidates Should Do Next

  • Revise core subjects: Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Science, and General Awareness on Current Affairs.
  • Practice previous years' RRB Group D papers and full-length mock tests.
  • Keep login credentials for rrbapply.gov.in ready for Aadhaar verification and e-call letter download.
  • Check the official RRB regional website regularly for exam city, date, and admit card updates specific to your phase.

RRB Group D Ajmer PET Exam Date 2026

The Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC), Jaipur has scheduled the PET for candidates shortlisted under CEN No. 08/2024 from 29 July to 31 July 2026, with 1 August 2026 kept as a final opportunity for candidates unable to appear earlier for valid reasons. RRB Group D PET Criteria 2026

The PET is qualifying in nature and must be completed successfully in a single attempt. Candidates who fail the first component are not permitted to attempt the second.

Category Requirement
Male Candidates Lift and carry 35 kg for 100 metres within 2 minutes, in a single chance, without dropping the weight
Run 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds, in a single chance
Female Candidates Lift and carry 20 kg for 100 metres within 2 minutes, in a single chance, without dropping the weight
Run 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds, in a single chance

Documents Required for RRB Group D PET 2026

  • PET e-call letter (printed copy)
  • Original photo ID proof
  • Original Aadhaar card
  • Any additional document specified in the zone-specific e-call letter

Document requirements may vary slightly by zone. Candidates should always check the instructions listed on their own e-call letter before travelling to the venue.

How to Download RRB Group D PET Admit Card 2026

  1. Visit the official website of the concerned RRC/RRB zone (e.g., rrcjaipur.in, rrb.digialm.com, rrchubli.in check the zone applicable to you).
  2. Look for the "RRB Group D PET Admit Card / e-Call Letter CEN 08/2024" link.
  3. Log in using your registration number and date of birth or password.
  4. Download and take a printout of the e-call letter.
  5. Carry the printed admit card along with the required documents to the PET venue.

The e-call letter is also sent via SMS and email to the registered mobile number and email ID of shortlisted candidates.

RRB Group D PET 2026: Important Instructions

  • Only candidates provisionally shortlisted after the CBT are eligible to appear for the PET.
  • Report to the venue at the reporting time mentioned on the e-call letter; late entry may not be permitted.
  • Both PET components (lift-and-carry and running) must be completed in a single attempt.
  • Candidates without a valid e-call letter and original ID/Aadhaar will not be allowed to appear.
  • PET is qualifying only; no marks are added to the final merit list.
  • Candidates found attempting to influence the RRC may have their candidature cancelled, and legal action may follow.
  • Keep checking the official RRC website of your zone regularly for venue, reporting time, and any date revisions.

They should be able to perform one preparatory tune and any of the notations i.e. Staff notation/ Tablature/ Tonic Solfa/ Hindustani/ Carnatic etc. Candidates must be able to tune individual instruments (in case of instruments require tuning) and match unknown notes on vocal or instruments.
  2. Candidates must have proficiency in playing any one instrument
  • Musical Experience Certificate –
  1. Grade 5th or equivalent or above in one instrument from a recognized music institute such as TCL or RSM, KM Music Conservatory, Bangalore School of Music, TSM, GMI, Berklee School of Music etc. OR
  2. Diploma or equivalent in the field of music for candidates performing Hindustani or Carnatic Classical Music from any recognized University. OR
  3. Certificate of participation/ awards presented at various events. For such candidates’ performance/ playing of blowing instruments with staff notation.
  • All candidates must read the official information completely before applying.

Indian Airforce Agniveer Vayu Musician Intake Online Form 2026 : Physical Eligibility Details

  • Height –
  1. For Male candidates: Minimum acceptable height is 162 cms.
  2. For Female candidates: Minimum acceptable height is 152 cms. For candidates belonging to North East or hilly regions of Uttarakhand, a lower minimum height of 147 cms will be accepted. In case of candidates from Lakshadweep, the minimum height will be 150 cms
  • Weight – Weight should be proportionate to height and age as applicable for IAF.
  • Chest –
  • For Male Candidates: The chest wall should be well proportioned and well developed. Minimum chest circumference should be 77 cms and the chest expansion should be at least 05 cms
  • For Female candidates: The chest wall should be well proportioned and well developed with the minimum range of expansion of 05 cms.
  1. Hearing – Candidate should have normal hearing i.e. able to hear forced whisper from a distance of 6 meters by each ear separately.
  2. Dental – Should have healthy gums, good set of teeth and minimum 14 dental points.
  • Visual Standards – 6/12 each eye, correctable to 6/6 each eye; Maximum limits of Refractive Error:- Hypermetropia: +2.0D, Myopia: 1D, Including ± 0.50 D Astigmatism & Colour Vision: CP-II
  • Physical Fitness Test (PFT) – PFT consists of a 1.6 Km run to be completed within 7 minutes (For Male Candidates) and 1.6 KM run to be completed within 8 minutes (For Female Candidates).
  • Candidates will have to complete 10 push-ups, 10 sit-ups and 20 squats Form (Male) & 10 sit-ups and 15 squats (Female).

How to Download the JSSC Field Worker Answer Key 2026

Once JSSC activates the answer key link, candidates can generally follow this process on the official portal. These are the standard steps JSSC uses across its recruitment exams; confirm the exact menu wording on the day the link goes live.

How to Raise an Objection Against the Answer Key

JSSC usually allows candidates to challenge the provisional answer key online if they find any error in a question or its marked answer. Based on how JSSC has run this process for other recent exams (such as JSSC ANM and JTMACCE), the general pattern is as follows.   • Objections are typically submitted online through the candidate login on the official JSSC website.
  • A specified per-question objection fee usually applies, along with supporting reference/proof for the claim.
  • Objections are only accepted within the window announced by JSSC and are not entertained after the deadline or through any other mode.
  • After reviewing all valid objections, JSSC releases the final answer key, which is then used to prepare the result.

How to Calculate Your Probable Score

You can get a rough estimate of your score using the provisional answer key, though your final score in the official result may differ after objections are reviewed.

  1. Download the JSSC Field Worker answer key PDF and your response sheet.
  2. Compare each of your marked answers against the official key, paper by paper.
  3. Count the number of correct and incorrect answers.
  4. Apply the marks-per-question and negative marking scheme once JSSC publishes it in the official notification, since this has not been independently confirmed here.

JSSC Field Worker Selection Process

The selection process for this recruitment consists of the following stages:

Only candidates who qualify Paper-I have their Paper-II evaluated, and only those who qualify Paper-II have their Paper-III evaluated.
  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates are called for verification of original certificates and documents.
  • Final Merit List: Prepared based on overall performance in the written examination and successful document verification.
